item.title: Nodex 0.5.5
item.description:
### Added
- Open and edit skills as pages. Customize groups skills by folder and shows which Agents read each one. Open a skill from a chat or the command palette, edit its instructions with changes saved directly to disk, or duplicate a read-only skill to make your own copy. - Mention skills in Pages with `$` or the Skills section of `@`. Click a mention to open the skill’s instructions. When you send the Page text to a chat, the mention becomes a skill invocation in the message.
- Nodex now coordinates your chats. One long-lived Nodex conversation routes every Inbox message knowing what is already running, watches the chats it starts, and keeps your Inbox focused on waiting messages and Pages waiting for you. Nodex adds a note when a Page needs more context, and one notification follows each episode. A chat can return a misrouted message with a reason for Nodex to route again. Reply to a Page waiting for you and your words go straight to its active chat, or answer the question it asked; open Nodex from the Inbox header to talk to it directly, and turn on Start my requests to let it start what you clearly ask for without a click. Work advances through Triage, Todo, In Progress and In Review as it starts and reports; your later Status choices take precedence. Accept reviewed work with `nodex page accept`; canceled work retires without releasing its dependents. - Pages have an Owner and one Assignee, either a person or an Agent. Board cards can wait for one another, and an Agent Assignee can be set to Start automatically. Cards, List rows, the Inbox and each Page’s Status say plainly whose move a Page waits for, such as Needs your answer, Ready for Alice’s review, Codex is working, Queued · 2nd or Waiting for NODEX-2. A Page’s Status offers Start, Resume, Accept or Open chat when you can act, while your later Status choices take precedence. Start hands a card to a chat Nodex watches, a card set to Start automatically starts once the cards it waits for are done, and for a bigger request Nodex can propose a plan that creates and starts its cards in one step. - Each Page’s Agent work in a Git Project gets its own branch and worktree, shared by its later chats. A new chat opens with its prompt while Nodex prepares the checkout. If preparation fails, the chat shows the reason and lets you retry. The Page shows its pull request and the GitHub threads it follows, the Board shows its pull request, and completing or canceling the Page removes the idle checkout while keeping the branch and PR link. - Work that starts without you, such as Automations and Pages set to start automatically, waits behind a limit you choose in Agents settings, initially four, and shows its place in the queue. Your own chats and the tasks they delegate never wait. - Pause Agent work for a Page, a Project, or the whole Space. Running work stops while queued messages and results wait for you to resume, including across restarts. - Your Agents can do what you can in Nodex. Ask a chat to start, pause, resume or accept work, set a card to Start automatically, set up an Automation that runs on its own or start one waiting for you in the Inbox, and History and Activity show it acted on your behalf. By default it asks before unattended work, leaves its own work for your review and leaves work you paused alone. - Watch GitHub from Settings → GitHub. Choose repositories and discover assignments, review requests and mentions. Updates on followed threads reach the Page's active chat, verified PR milestones move its stage, and new GitHub requests arrive in the Inbox for your decision. Nodex can acknowledge a request and post its result back to its GitHub origin. Problems in the Inbox offer a fix, and Activity explains routing, milestones, delivery and recovery. Polling, delivery and replies resume safely after restart. - Work with other people in a team Space. Join one from the account menu at the bottom of the rail, then switch between Spaces there or from the command palette, moving between a team's Pages, Boards and Inbox alongside your personal Space; each Space keeps its own layout, and losing access to a team leaves personal work untouched. Settings → Spaces shows who is in the Space and which devices reach it: Owners invite people, revoke Devices, remove Members and rename the Space, and everyone links and revokes their own Devices. Remote access lets your phone and other computers reach your personal Space without sharing it. Connections pin the host's certificate and resume live after a dropped network. History records who made each change, and each person keeps their own Inbox, unread chats, pins, reminders and View preferences across devices. - Run a team Space on an always-on machine with `nodex serve`. It initializes the Space, its Owner and certificate, runs Agents, Sources and Automations without desktop windows, and keeps working while everyone's laptops are closed. Members start chats and work on the host from their desktops and phones and use hosted chats as they would their own: attach images, files and Pages, fork, open side chats and edit their last message. The person who started a chat and the Space's Owners rename, archive, compact or stop it, and questions and approvals stay with the Member entitled to answer them. Host status reports when Agents share the host account's file access.
- Claude Fable 5.2 is available, and new Claude models appear as soon as your Claude Code offers them. Claude chats list the models your installed Claude Code offers your account, with their effort, Fast and Ultracode choices, without waiting for a Nodex update. The default Fable model and the name `fable` follow the Fable model Claude Code gives you; Fable 5.2 needs Claude Code 2.1.321 or newer. - See how an agent understood your request without going back to its chat. When you send a message and move on, the agent's opening statement, what it says it will do before it starts, appears briefly at the top of the window you are in. Point at it to read all of it, Stop the agent or Reply to correct it on the spot, or click it to open the chat. A working chat's hover card in the sidebar shows the same statement. Turn it off in Settings → General → Notifications.
### Changed
- The Page open beside a chat is no longer sent with every message. The Composer shows it as a dashed suggestion; click it to send a link to that Page, and the Blocks you selected, with your next message, and click again to take it back. Each new message starts without it. - A chat without a Project now has a folder of its own from the start. Open a Terminal or Files in a new chat before sending anything, and the first message runs in that same folder. The project menu shows where the chat will work and lets you choose an existing folder instead; new folders live under `Chats` in your Nodex folder and are named after non-English prompts too. Once started, the chat's summary shows its folder, and Turn into project makes that folder a Project without moving anything. Deleting a chat removes its folder only when Nodex created it and it is still empty. - Agents hear from the tasks they delegate while they keep working. A delegated task's question or result reaches its Agent at the next pause between tools instead of after its whole reply, and Claude Code no longer stops its running tools to take one in. Waiting on one task also returns for another task's question, and answering a task that already finished says plainly that it starts follow-up work. A question the Agent leaves unanswered is handed to you. - The Inbox's History is now part of Activity, one timeline of everything handled in that Inbox. Each message you send to a chat, file, keep or finish is a single line beside what Nodex, your Automations and GitHub did, and All, Messages, Nodex & automations and Problems narrow it down. Expand a message's line to read it, see why it went where it did, and open its chat, return it to the Inbox, mark it done or delete it. A chat it went to shows its live state on the line while the work is under way. - Scheduled tasks are now Automations. Keep the same schedules, runbooks, waiting Inbox runs and history, and choose Dry run, Ask first or Run; only an Automation’s Owner, or an Agent working for them, can let it run on its own. Automations can also react to GitHub events: a dry run records each judgement and its reason, Ask first proposes work in the Owner’s Inbox, and Run starts Pages under a standing grant. - Nodex Mobile now links to each of your Spaces as one of your Devices, team Spaces included. Scan the code from Settings → Spaces → Link a device, switch between linked Spaces on the phone, and keep working in a team Space while its host runs, even with your laptop closed. Capture to your personal or team Inbox, start chats, answer your Page’s questions, accept reviewed work and follow chats live with every picture in them. Each Space is reachable at its local, Tailscale or DNS address over a connection pinned to that Space’s certificate, and on iPhone it tells you only about what is yours to answer, while you're away from your computer. Removing the phone’s Device ends its access immediately. Settings > Mobile is gone; link a phone you paired before again from Settings → Spaces. - Nodex Mobile has a menu for where you're looking. Tap the Space's avatar, or swipe right across the Inbox, to choose the Library's Inbox or any Project's, see how many messages wait in each, and switch to another linked Space. Choosing an Inbox no longer means opening the Composer first, each Space remembers the one you chose, and the Composer says which Project a thought will go to. - Side chats now stay with the chat they came from. Closing a side chat's tab, quitting or restarting no longer discards it: its tab comes back where you left it after a restart, a closed side chat reopens from the chat's summary, and `Delete side chat` in its tab menu removes it for good. Closing a side chat no longer asks for confirmation. Side chats of remote conversations remain temporary. - Side chat tabs and tool tabs such as Plan, Automation, Subagents and process output can be dragged like any other tab. Reorder them, move them to another tab group or the bottom panel, or drop them on a group's edge to split it; tool tabs stay in the right panel. - Clicking a file attached in a Page now opens it, instead of a small details popup. A file saved in the Page opens in a tab beside the Page, just like from the Page's Files list, so Markdown renders, HTML reports show as pages, and images, PDFs and media play. A linked file opens in Files. Right-click a file for Open in new tab, Save… and Copy reference, and press Enter on a selected file to open it. In Page history and other read-only previews, a file opens in a viewer that shows the version that was captured.
### Removed
- Save as chat is gone from side chats, which now keep their conversation on their own.
### Fixed
- On iOS 27, tapping a button in Nodex Mobile's top bar no longer also scrolls the list beneath it to the top. Opening Settings used to leave the Inbox at its oldest message.
- Older chats open again after upgrading Nodex.
- Dropping a tab on the edge of a tab group now splits the group instead of doing nothing. - Page history opens again after you edit a Page and pause. The automatic revision Nodex saves when you stop editing made the Page's history show a database error instead of its revisions. - Usage analytics that is off when Nodex starts no longer sends events an earlier launch left waiting. Setting `DO_NOT_TRACK`, or otherwise turning analytics off while Nodex was closed, now discards them as turning it off in Settings does. - Agent settings edits through symbolic links apply reliably, including immediately after startup or after a link points to a new file. - A heartbeat's unread dot in Automations clears once you open its chat. It used to stay forever, because only a cron run opened from its folder was marked read. Any finished run is now read as soon as its chat is on screen, however you got there. - Heartbeats run on their schedule. An hourly heartbeat ran about every 90 minutes, and one set to every few minutes waited half an hour between runs, because Nodex postponed each one after its own previous run. A heartbeat now waits only while its chat is busy, and counts its interval from when the previous run started, so a long run no longer pushes the next one back. Heartbeats an hour or more apart start within five minutes either side of their time. - Every Agent can now set up and change Automations, reorder Sidebar Sections and manage a chat's queued messages, not only Codex. Claude Code never saw these Nodex tools, and its heartbeats now stay quiet unless something needs you. - Browser tools that sit over a web page show again. The annotation composer, the device toolbar's resize handles and the offer to save a password were hidden behind the page, as was the sidebar when it slid over a full-width Browser.
